gen_risks.description: Armed conflicts, civil unrest, and security crises in FCV regions (such as North-West/South-West Cameroon and CAR) threaten project execution and health service delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare and implement country-specific Security Risk Assessments and Security Management Plans, adapt flexible operational protocols, and closely coordinate with local authorities.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence, leading to large population displacements.

gen_risks.description: Recurrent climate shocks, including major flooding events and extreme weather, increase vulnerability to waterborne disease outbreaks and damage health infrastructure.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate adaptation and green/resilient standards into facility refurbishments, establish early warning systems, and update emergency preparedness plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change contributed to at least 50 percent of natural disasters registered in Cameroon, CAR, Chad, and RoC... mostly constituted of floods

gen_risks.description: Challenging macro-fiscal conditions, heavy national debt burdens, and low domestic health budget allocations risk delaying project co-funding and long-term financial sustainability.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to strengthen Domestic Resource Mobilization, establish Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, and explore public-private partnerships.
gen_risks.evidence: A challenging macro-fiscal outlook and high poverty levels make the region particularly vulnerable to shocks

gen_risks.description: Weak institutional procurement capacity and limited market competition in fragile settings create substantial contract management delays and market bottlenecks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy qualified procurement specialists, provide fiduciary training, adopt fit-for-purpose flexible procurement in FCV areas, and utilize STEP for real-time tracking.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: High volume of decentralized workshops, local training sessions, and field operations creates risks of questionable or undocumented financial expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Disseminate standardized financial manuals down to local implementation partners, customize accounting software, and conduct regular internal and external financial audits.
gen_risks.evidence: several activities under the project like workshops, trainings and the local-level capacity building are at risk to generate questionable expenditures in Cameroon.

gen_risks.description: Expansion of laboratory diagnostics and healthcare interventions risks generating hazardous medical waste, toxic chemical residues, and biological contamination.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and implement healthcare waste management plans, mandate biosafety and biosecurity protocols, and train laboratory personnel on safe waste disposal.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used.

gen_risks.description: Expanded deployment of health workers and community-level staff in target areas carries substantial risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit dedicated GBV specialists, enforce strict institutional codes of conduct, establish GBV-sensitive grievance redress mechanisms, and execute country SEA/SH Action Plans.
gen_risks.evidence: The increased presence of new health workforce such as Community Health Workers... may create concerns of Sexual exploitation and abuse within communities.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement during project rollout risks excluding vulnerable, mobile, or marginalized populations (such as IDPs, refugees, and indigenous groups).
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement country-tailored Stakeholder Engagement Plans, deploy accessible Grievance Redress Mechanisms, and conduct targeted community outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to: (i) inadequate stakeholder engagement... (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

gen_risks.description: Outbreaks of public health emergencies risk diverting resources and medical personnel, causing severe disruptions in routine essential primary healthcare services.
gen_risks.mitigation: Formulate and update health facility contingency plans, expand epidemic-ready primary healthcare networks, and routinely monitor routine service utilization indicators.
gen_risks.evidence: after Cameroon's first COVID-19 case in March 2020, outpatient visits fell by 7 percent, immunizations dropped 5-7 percent

gen_risks.description: Systemic gender barriers, mobility constraints, and domestic responsibilities restrict women's access to technical field epidemiology (FETP/FELTP) and veterinary training.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement proactive female candidate recruitment, offer flexible modular training formats, set gender targets, and conduct gender gap assessments across IHR core capacities.
gen_risks.evidence: women dominate low-paid frontline roles but are largely absent from technical positions... partly due to limited access to training programs

gen_risks.description: Highly porous borders coupled with refugee movements and migration create significant risks of unchecked cross-border transmission of infectious diseases.
gen_risks.mitigation: Execute regional agreements for cross-border data sharing, establish surveillance and health facilities at Points of Entry (PoEs), and conduct joint cross-border simulations.
gen_risks.evidence: HeSP-3 countries... face similar health security challenges driven by porous borders, displacement and frequent cross-border movement

gen_risks.description: Rapid escalation of Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) due to improper antibiotic usage threatens treatment efficacy and elevates mortality across human and animal health.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize National Action Plans for AMR, establish stewardship programs in health facilities, enforce regulatory guidelines on antibiotic use, and improve AMR surveillance.
gen_risks.evidence: Central Africa is also significantly burdened by antimicrobial resistance (AMR). For instance, in CAR, the mortality rate associated with AMR is among the highest

gen_risks.description: Interoperable digital disease surveillance platforms and cross-border information sharing pose risks regarding personal data protection breaches and ethical data security.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish clear legal guidelines and technical standards for processing personal health data in alignment with national privacy laws and international best practices.
gen_risks.evidence: inadequate attention to ensure that guidelines established under the Program include considerations for and ethical data security protocols;

gen_risks.description: Time-sensitive legal covenants requiring staffing, accounting software customization, and external auditor recruitment within tight post-effectiveness windows risk non-compliance delays.
gen_risks.mitigation: Initiate early recruitment processes during project preparation, utilize Project Preparation Advances where available, and closely track legal covenant compliance.
gen_risks.evidence: The Recipient shall, no later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, recruit an external auditor... customize existing accounting software

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
